correctness.rationale: For each center simplex, square-freeness makes every lower face of size at least two exclusive to that center. Decreasing-size pairing with the chosen root makes each lower face free with a unique codimension-one coface. The residue is exactly the root-star union. Square-freeness also makes target edges unique; connectedness follows by replacing every length-two step through a center by a two-edge walk through its chosen root. The edge count then gives cycle rank \(e-v+1\) on both components. The packaged verifier independently validates all collapse conditions on 1,501 labeled small graphs and three projective-plane incidence graphs. The finite tests are not used as the proof.

value.rationale: The result gives an explicit and reproducible simple-homotopy reduction for an infinite arbitrary-degree class, not merely an abstract homotopy type. The bipartite case is structurally distinct from the nonbipartite square-free case because the neighborhood complex splits into two components; the theorem identifies both embedded spines and their exact common cycle rank. This supplies concrete models for high-degree examples such as projective-plane incidence graphs and can support computations requiring an actual subcomplex rather than only a homotopy equivalence.
